attrs.management_says: Revenue growth driven by $176.8M (33.2%) increase in direct-to-consumer sales (18 new stores, ecommerce) and $10.2M (22.8%) license revenue growth.
attrs.numbers_show: Total revenue grew $497.2M (27.1%). Cited drivers sum to $187M, covering only 37.6% of growth. The remaining ~$310M (wholesale) is unexplained in the provided MD&A. Receivables grew 19.6% vs revenue 27.1%; DSO improved 35→33 days annually, but quarterly DSO worsened in Q1 (46→48) and improved sharply in Q4 (32→28). Operating cash flow dropped 40% ($199.8M→$120.1M) while net income rose 26%.
attrs.verdict: explanation does not fit the numbers

attrs.reason: Management's stated drivers (DTC +$176.8M, license +$10.2M) sum to $187M, covering only 37.6% of the $497.2M revenue increase. The remaining ~$310M is not attributed to any driver in the provided MD&A. Segment data (E55) shows North America revenue grew $467M but does not break out wholesale vs DTC; the MD&A links North America growth to the same consolidated drivers, not providing a separate wholesale driver.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: The $310M of revenue growth not attributed to DTC or license channels is wholesale revenue within the North America segment, which grew $467.0M (E55) and, combined with $30.1M international growth (E55), accounts for the total $497.2M increase (E13, E1). The MD&A states North America growth was "primarily due to the items discussed above in the Consolidated Results of Operations" (E55), linking it to the same demand drivers. The quarterly DSO patterns (E27-E30) reflect seasonal shipment timing (Q4 revenue surge 35% with DSO improving to 28 days) rather than collection deterioration.

attrs.final_verdict: explanation does not fit the numbers
